newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P says monitoring Nissan Life's situation.
newsitem.headline: S&P says monitoring Nissan Life's situation.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Monday it is cautiously monitoring the situation of Nissan Mutual Life Insurance, which will be taken over by a new firm under a framework developed by an industry body.
"In the short term, there will be no additional burden on (Nissan Life) policyholders," said Keiko Mizuguchi, associate director of insurance ratings at S&P.
"There might be more (burdens on policyholders) in the medium to longer term. Of course, we will be monitoring developments in the industry," she told a news conference.

S&P also said in a statement it views the impact of Japan's "Big Bang" financial liberalisation as generally positive for the industry over the long term. But over the short term, there is likely to be considerable pressure on some insurance companies, it said.
The statement said the Big Bang is likely to lead to consolidation in the industry in line with the establishment of holding companies.
Moreover, it said insurance companies operating within a holding company structure will place greater importance on profitability.
The holding company environment will also encourage companies to create new structures able to facilitate specialised services, it said.

The Big Bang provision for allowing banks to market insurance products will be more limited than expected because banks will be permitted only to offer life and long-term fire insurance policies, it said.
Nevertheless, deregulation should have a long-term positive impact as distribution channels become increasingly liberalised and companies offer more competitive products, it said.
